frame.subtitle: {type}
frame.held: An administrator is holding this Endpoint. It cannot be deleted.

list.emptyText: An Endpoint is a device or a network that gets its DNS from Ctrl Z. Start with one.
list.exportFailed: The export could not be made. Try again.

partial.title: Not every Endpoint was loaded
partial.text: The list may be missing Endpoints, so selecting all is off until it loads.
partial.retryAria: Try again: load the rest of the Endpoints

selection.overflow: Only the first {max} Endpoints go into this action.

edit.title: Edit {name}
edit.held: An administrator is holding this Endpoint. It does not answer and cannot be deleted until it is released.

rotate.title: New resolver ID
rotate.text: The Resolver ID and the DoH token change. You have to set the devices up again, and the share and download links of this Endpoint stop working.
rotate.buttonAria: Get a new Resolver ID for {name}
rotate.confirmText: The current ID stops working, and devices set up with it get no DNS until you set them up again. The share and download links of this Endpoint end too.
rotate.done: New ID created. Set the devices up again.

fields.namesHint: One name per line, or separated by commas. Up to 50 names, 64 characters each.
fields.name: Name
fields.profileTwoHint: Profile 2 applies after the first one.

analyticsHint.some: Only counts and the overall result are kept, with no domains.
analyticsHint.full: The domain and the result of every query are kept.

statusHint.pending: It turns active with the first DNS query.
statusHint.soft_disabled: The filter does not apply, and DNS answers like an ordinary resolver.
statusHint.hard_disabled: Nothing is answered, and devices have no DNS.

fields.legacyHint: Devices with no encrypted DNS reach DNS from your IP address. Off until you turn it on.
fields.secureDnsHint: The address of anyone who queries over DoH correctly joins the authorized IPs.
fields.ddnsHint: The addresses of the hosts you register join the authorized IPs.
fields.exposeIpHint: The outside IP of a device can be seen with a DNS query.
fields.requireIpsHint: Only addresses in the Authorized IPs list get answers. The list needs at least one address.
fields.requireIpsWarning: Once this is on, devices on an address that is not in the list get no answer.

delete.title: Delete {name}
delete.text: Devices set up with "{name}" get no DNS after it is deleted, and their internet may stop working. This cannot be undone.
delete.batchText: Devices set up with these Endpoints get no DNS after they are deleted, and their internet may stop working. This cannot be undone.
delete.confirm: I know the devices lose DNS
delete.heldText: An administrator holds these Endpoints, so they cannot be deleted: {names}. Take them out of the selection.
delete.heldRefused: These Endpoints cannot be deleted now, because they are held or an address is suspended: {names}.
delete.freeDnsOn: Devices that use our Plain DNS addresses from a network of this Endpoint are no longer identified. They keep getting free DNS, without any filter.
delete.freeDnsOff: Devices that use our Plain DNS addresses from a network of this Endpoint are no longer identified, and their queries are refused.

group.name: Group name
group.pickHint: Optional. The Endpoints you tick move into this group.
group.selected: {count, plural, one {# Endpoint selected} other {# Endpoints selected}}
group.limit: A group takes at most {max, number} Endpoints at a time. Move the rest into it later.
group.deleteText: The group goes and its Endpoints stay, with no group.

move.title: Move {count, plural, one {# Endpoint} other {# Endpoints}}
move.done: {count, plural, one {# Endpoint moved.} other {# Endpoints moved.}}

batch.title: Edit {count, plural, one {# Endpoint} other {# Endpoints}}
batch.done: {count, plural, one {# Endpoint edited.} other {# Endpoints edited.}}

locks.tooMany: This change needs the lock passwords of more than 8 profiles. Change fewer Endpoints at a time.

destinations.title: Destinations are lost
destinations.text: With this change some destinations of the profile are not available on these Endpoints, and they act like "Bypass". Continue?

missing.title: Endpoint not found
missing.text: This Endpoint does not exist or is gone.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.hint: Drag with a mouse. On touch, tap the start time and then the end time. With a keyboard, use the arrow keys and Enter. Select a window to edit it.
schedule.announceStart: Start set on {day} at {time}. Choose the end time and press Enter.
schedule.tooMany: At most {max, number} windows are allowed.

copy.title: Copy day
copy.note: The windows of the chosen days are replaced by those of the source day. Nothing changes until you save.

schedule.unsaved: Not saved: {count, plural, one {# window} other {# windows}}
schedule.none: No windows. The Endpoint always uses its own profile.

window.title: Window
window.endBeforeStart: The end has to be after the start.

clients.title: Clients
clients.groupCountSoFar: {count, plural, one {# client so far} other {# clients so far}}
clients.emptyText: Clients appear on their own with the first request of each device. You can also make one by hand.

selection.loaded: Only the clients loaded so far can be selected. To remove all of them use Delete all clients.

row.nothingKnown: Nothing is known about this device yet

dialog.label: Label
dialog.labelHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Left empty, it is made from the name.
dialog.labelVisible: The label crosses the network unencrypted when a device connects (DoT, DoQ), and so does one made from the name. Do not put a person’s name in either.

delete.titleIds: Delete {count, plural, one {# client} other {# clients}}
delete.textIds: {count, plural, one {# client} other {# clients}} will be deleted.
delete.textInactive: {count, plural, one {# client has} other {# clients have}} sent no request for over {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} and will be deleted.
delete.textAll: All {count, plural, one {# client} other {# clients}} of this Endpoint will be deleted.
delete.note: A client that sends a request again is seen again, but its own name and profile do not come back.
delete.confirm: I know this cannot be undone.
delete.progress: {count, plural, one {# client} other {# clients}} deleted…
delete.done: {count, plural, one {# client} other {# clients}} deleted.

ips.title: Addresses
ips.intro: These are the addresses that get DNS from this Endpoint: Plain DNS addresses and Authorized IPs.

claims.title: Plain DNS addresses
claims.text: Devices with no encrypted DNS are recognised by these addresses.
claims.emptyText: Add an address or a subnet so its Plain DNS requests reach this Endpoint.
claims.releaseText: The address is taken off the Endpoint, and the devices behind it are no longer filtered.
claims.legacyOff: Requests from these addresses do not reach the Endpoint until Plain DNS is on.
claims.graceNote: Addresses that are not proven have a grace period. Prove them before it ends or they are suspended.

claim.title: Add a Plain DNS address
claim.intro: Enter the address or subnet your devices reach DNS from.
claim.useMineNote: The address the panel sees for this browser can differ from the one a device's DNS comes from (a carrier network, IPv6).
claim.needsAdmin: This address needs an administrator's approval.

proof.title: Prove {cidr}
proof.readFailed: The addresses could not be read. Close this window and open it again.
proof.gone: This address is no longer there.
proof.suspended: This address is suspended and cannot be proven. Contact support.
proof.needsAdmin: Proof alone does not finish this address: it waits for an administrator.
proof.intro: For {cidr} you have to show that a DNS request comes from this network.
proof.noZone: The service domain is not set yet, so proof is not possible.
proof.noPair: This Endpoint has no DNS addresses yet.
proof.waiting: From the network {cidr}, do one of the three ways. It is checked every 3 seconds.

tcp.title: TCP
tcp.text: Send a TXT query over TCP. There is nothing to type.

udp.title: UDP
udp.text: Send the query over UDP and type the TXT answer here.
udp.seen: A UDP query was seen. Type the code from the TXT answer.

secure.title: Secure DNS
secure.text: On a device that uses this Endpoint's encrypted DNS, press the button so the browser asks for the name.

proof.expires: {seconds, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}} until the code ends
proof.noProofCodeText: The code is not right, or the query reached us from another address. Check the code and try again. If the query came from another address, get a new code.
proof.noProofText: The query reached us from another address, usually the provider's resolver or another path. This code can no longer prove the address: get a new one and run the query again from the device whose address you claimed.
proof.unavailable: This address is shared with other networks, so it cannot be proven for you. Use encrypted DNS (DoH or DoT) instead: it needs no address.

authorized.title: Authorized IPs
authorized.requireOn: Require Authorized IPs is on: only these addresses get answers, and the last one cannot be deleted.
authorized.emptyText: Add an address or subnet that must always get answers.
authorized.currentWhy: This is your current address and cannot be deleted.
authorized.lastWhy: While Require Authorized IPs is on, the last address cannot be deleted.

add.title: Add an Authorized IP
add.hint: One address to a line, or separated by commas. Up to {max, number}. Widest allowed: /16 for IPv4, /32 for IPv6.
add.outOfRange: Too wide: at most /16 for IPv4 and /32 for IPv6.
add.done: {count, plural, one {# address} other {# addresses}} added.

delete.title: Delete {count, plural, one {# address} other {# addresses}}
delete.text: These addresses will stop getting answers.

ddns.title: Dynamic DNS hosts
ddns.text: The address these names point to becomes an Authorized IP on its own. It never counts as proof of a Plain DNS address.
ddns.deleteText: The addresses that came from this host are removed from the Authorized IPs too.

remind.title: The network of your last sign-in is not added
remind.text: You last signed in to the panel from <tech>{ip}</tech>, and this Endpoint holds no address that covers it. A device on that network that types our Plain DNS addresses gets free DNS without your filters. Add the address to filter it.

ipv6.title: The service addresses are IPv6
ipv6.on: Plain DNS cannot be matched to an Endpoint over IPv6, because only IPv4 networks can be added. A device that types these addresses gets free DNS without your filters. Use DoH, DoT or DoQ to be filtered.
ipv6.off: Plain DNS cannot be matched to an Endpoint over IPv6, because only IPv4 networks can be added. A device that types these addresses is refused. Use DoH, DoT or DoQ.

legacyOff.on: With Plain DNS off, devices that reach DNS from these addresses are no longer identified. If they still use our addresses, they get free DNS without your filters.
legacyOff.off: With Plain DNS off, devices that reach DNS from these addresses are no longer identified, and a query from them is refused.
